correctness.rationale: The Wolfram Rule 28 local outputs 1 exactly on 010,011,100; de Bruijn Z/O matrices enumerate closed indexed cyclic paths, including n=1 and n=2. Z³=Z² and tr Z=tr Z²=2 give zero-output fiber count. Restricting OZ^r to the nonzero two-state block gives E (zero gap) and F (positive gap), so every output fiber has the displayed trace product. With all positive gaps, trace(F^k)=Lucas L_k and k≤floor(n/2). Zero gaps either create E²=0 or permit pairing EF=diag(1,0)≤F entrywise; nonnegative trace-product monotonicity yields strict suboptimality, including the lone odd-ring boundary via Fibonacci F_m<L_m. Hence exactly the two alternating even winners or n rotations of the unique length-two zero-gap odd winner, with short n≤3 direct cases. Independent exhaustive direct-map counts through n=12 corroborated every output fiber; the matrix proof handles all n.
